Title: GitHub repo visualizer — see any repo as a map | Visual Anything
URL: https://visualanything.com/github-repo-visualizer
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
GitHub repo visualizer — see any repo as a map | Visual Anything

# See any GitHub repo as a map.

Paste a public GitHub link and Visual Anything draws the repository: its folders, its files, and which file imports which. Explore it in 2D or 3D, click any file to read it.

## Folders and files, as a tree

The repository is the centre; its folders branch out and their files hang off them. Big folders fold into one bubble you can open.

## Imports between files

Point at a file to see what it imports and what imports it - or show every import line at once.

## Read the code in place

Click a file to open it beside the map, with the part you clicked lit up.

## Its recent history

Step back through the recent commits and watch files appear, change and go.

Tip: a link like visualanything.com/app?repo=owner/repo opens that repository straight away (it asks first).

## Good to know

### Does it work with private repos?

It reads public GitHub repositories. For your own private code, open the folder on your computer instead - it never leaves your device.

### Do I need an account?

No. Making and exploring maps is free and needs no account.

Title: Atlas - any GitHub repo as an interactive map
URL: https://corvidlabs.github.io/fledge-plugin-atlas/
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
Atlas - any GitHub repo as an interactive map

# See any GitHub repo as a living map.

 Atlas reads a project's specs, source, and git history and draws one interactive picture: a spec and code graph, a coverage treemap and sunburst, a dependency DAG, a churn-vs-coverage view, and more. The whole engine is compiled to WebAssembly and runs right here on the page. 

Private repo, or hitting rate limits? Add a token (optional)

 Anonymous requests share GitHub's 60-per-hour limit. Paste a personal access token (classic, with `repo` scope for private repos, or no scope for public) to get 5,000 per hour. It is stored only in this browser and sent only to api.github.com.

Title: RepoGraph — Understand any codebase in minutes
URL: https://repograph.dev/
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
RepoGraph — Understand any codebase in minutes

# Understand any codebase in minutes, not weeks.

Drop in a GitHub URL. Get an interactive map of the architecture, ask questions in plain English, and jump from any answer straight to the code behind it.

No credit card · public & private repos

RepoGraph Drag to explore the map

...

## Getting started

From URL to understanding, in four steps.

1 Drop in a repo URL

Paste any GitHub link on your dashboard — we clone, parse, and embed it, ready in a few minutes.

github.com/testuser/testapp Add repository

testuser/demoapp Ready

2 Skim the essentials

Stars, languages, README, contributors, and recent commits at a glance.

testuser/demoapp 2.3k stars · 41 contributors

3 Explore the graph

An interactive map of modules, functions, and classes — zoom, filter, and trace how they depend on each other.

+−

4 Chat with citations

Ask in plain English. Answers cite file and line, and every citation opens the code viewer at that exact spot.

✦ RepoGraph Sessions are cookie-based JWTs issued in auth.py:42.

...

## How it works

What happens between the paste and the map.

Clone

A shallow git clone of your repo, plus GitHub metadata — stars, README, contributors, recent commits.

Parse & chunk

`tree-sitter` reads every source file and splits it into function, class, and block chunks.

Embed

Each chunk becomes a 768-dimension vector in `pgvector`, so questions can find code by meaning, not just keywords.

Build the graph

Call, import, inheritance, render, and definition relationships become the nodes and edges you explore.

Answer with citations

Chat retrieves the most relevant chunks and replies with citations that link back to the exact lines.

Title: RepoSense: Visualize Your Repo Cinematically
URL: https://ilevytate.github.io/reposense/
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
RepoSense: Visualize Your Repo Cinematically

# RepoSense

Visualize your repo cinematically

 Every file becomes a tower. Every folder becomes a terrace. The whole repository assembles itself into a structure you can fly through: sized by bytes, coloured by language, lit by how recently it changed. 

 Options 

 Deep history scan Replays recent commits to recover per-file churn and a real growth timeline, at one API request per commit. On by default; without a token it stops at 40 commits to stay inside the anonymous rate limit. 

Commits to replay 250

250

 GitHub token (optional) Raises the rate limit from 60 to 5,000 requests/hour and unlocks private repositories. Stored only in this browser's local storage and sent only to api.github.com. ghp_… / github_pat_… 

Drop a `reposense.json`

Private repos, full git history, no API limits. Generate one locally:

## Controls

- Drag orbit
- Scroll zoom
- Right-drag pan
- 1 2 3 switch mode
- T play the tour
- R start / stop recording
- P save a PNG
- F focus the search box
- Space play / pause the timeline
- 0 reset the view
- Esc clear selection · stop the tour
- Shift+click open the file on GitHub

## Reading the structure

- Ring: how deep a file sits in the tree
- Terrace: a directory; everything it contains stands on it
- Height: file size, on a log scale
- Colour: language
- Glow: churn, when history is available

## Chronology

- Bars: commit activity per period; the played span is lit
- White flare: a file at the moment of its creation
- Playhead: drag it, or press Space to replay the history

# Visualize any GitHub repository 

 Explore file structures with interactive treemaps, analyze commit activity, discover top contributors, and understand codebases at a glance. 

 facebook/react microsoft/vscode vuejs/vue torvalds/linux 

## Powerful visualization tools

Everything you need to understand a codebase

### Interactive Treemap

Visualize file structure with D3.js treemaps. Click to drill down into folders, see file sizes at a glance.

### Commit Activity

See commit frequency over time with beautiful bar charts. Understand project momentum and development pace.

### Language Breakdown

Donut chart showing programming language distribution. Instantly see what technologies power the project.

### Top Contributors

Discover who's building the project. See contributor avatars, commit counts, and profile links.

### Export Options

Export treemap as PNG image, download file data as CSV or JSON for further analysis.

### Dark & Light Themes

Switch between themes with a click or press T. Follows your system preference by default.

## How it works

Three simple steps to explore any repository

1

### Paste Repository URL

Enter any public GitHub repo URL in the search bar above

2

### Automatic Analysis

GitScope fetches file tree, commits, contributors via GitHub API

3

### Explore & Export

Interact with visualizations, drill down folders, export data

...

JavaScript D3.js Chart.js GitHub API PWA Ready

...

### Features

- Interactive Treemap: Visualize file sizes and commit activity with drill-down navigation
- Contributor Insights: See who contributes most and identify "bus factor" risks
- File Intelligence: Find abandoned files, most changed files, and largest files
- Language Breakdown: View repository language composition
- Search & Filter: Filter by author, file type, or date range
- Export: Save treemap as PNG or share via URL

### Technology

 GitScope is built entirely with vanilla JavaScript — no frameworks, no build steps. It uses D3.js for treemap visualizations and Chart.js for charts. 

### API Rate Limits

 GitScope uses the unauthenticated GitHub API, which allows 60 requests per hour. Each repository analysis uses approximately 6-8 requests. For best results, use on small to medium-sized repositories. 

### Open Source

 GitScope is open source under the MIT License. View the source code and contribute at GitHub. 

 GitScope does not collect, store, or transmit any personal data. All repository data is fetched directly from GitHub's API to your browser and is not stored on any server.
